paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Jesus doesn't wait for the widow to ask. She never says a word to Him in this whole passage. He sees her, and the Lord "had compassion on her" (Luke 7:13). Her grief was the only invitation He needed.

Now look at how He answers it. He tells her, "Do not weep," and then He backs it up by touching the coffin and saying, "Young man, I tell you, get up!" (Luke 7:13-14). Nobody else in that crowd could say those words and mean them. I've said "stay in the oven a little longer" to a lot of dough, and the dough NEVER listened! When Jesus speaks, even death has to hear it.

So when you're standing at your own gate with something you can't fix, remember who walked up to that coffin. He sees you, He cares, and He has power over the very thing that has you stuck. The people said, "God has visited His people!" (Luke 7:16), and that's the good news you carry out of here. This is one of the ways Jesus shows who He is, and it's why I keep my ovens ready.
